column3: Close to the Hebrew; “why do the nations plot” is rendered “Why are the nations in an uproar.”
“They sit together” is rendered “take counsel together.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB capitalizes “My King.”
NASB adds “surely” to “I will tell,” and capitalizes “My Son.”
“Let me make the nations your inheritance” is rendered “I will surely give the nations as Your inheritance”; “surely” and “very” are added.
Close to the Hebrew; “like a potter's vessel” is rendered “like earthenware.”
“Act prudently” is rendered “show discernment,” “be instructed” as “Take warning,” and “rulers” as “judges.”
“Kiss the son” is rendered “Do homage to the Son,” and “for His anger burns in a little” as “His wrath may soon be kindled.”
